correctness.rationale: Projector calculation supplies every matrix entry for all p<=q and all steps. Exact rational derivatives show r and (1-r)/z are strictly decreasing; all off-diagonal entries are positive. Spectral ordering identifies the smaller-class diagonal, which decreases uniquely from 1 to 2/(p+q)-1. A uniform O(1/q) bound against r(t) proves q times the critical dimensionless step tends to the unique positive numerator root, with O(1/q) error. 3 symbolic identities, 4100 exact rational entries, 310 numerical horizons and representative asymptotic checks pass; the universal conclusion rests on proof, not finite runs.

value.rationale: Exact timestep positivity matters for nonnegative diffusion probabilities despite A-stable high-order integration. This family-wide result exposes a diagonal-only obstruction, identifies the weaker class and yields one sharp interval, plus a degree-scaled constant independent of extreme partition imbalance. This is a structural stability-boundary benchmark beyond basic scalar Padé sign observations or generic small-step sufficiency.
